title: Rapid Deprovisioning & Sequester Exhibit (Draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:

This Exhibit defines the procedures, timelines, and evidentiary obligations for (a) rapid deprovisioning of Redwood Inference access to Customer Data and Customer Systems, and (b) temporary or long-term sequester (isolation) of data and model artifacts under events that materially impair the mutual ability to operate (collectively, "Sequester Events"). It is intended to be attached to the Master Services Agreement ("MSA") or Data Processing Agreement ("DPA") and controls to the extent of any conflict.

This is a working template intended for negotiation; placeholder sections (e.g., time windows, thresholds) should be filled per customer risk posture.

Definitions (selected):
- "Deprovisioning": immediate removal of operational access (user accounts, API keys, service credentials, IAM roles) used by Redwood personnel and/or Redwood-managed infrastructure to access Customer Data or systems.
- "Sequester": the technical and legal isolation of specific datasets, model weights, logs, or backups such that routine processing and serving are suspended or restricted, while ensuring integrity and evidentiary preservation.
- "Sequester Event": any of the following: (i) verified data breach attributable to Redwood; (ii) lawful government order requiring suspension; (iii) Customer suspension or termination for cause; (iv) material dispute over data ownership or regulatory noncompliance; (v) other mutually agreed triggers.
- "Custody Window": timeframe during which Redwood retains an encrypted snapshot for potential restoration or evidence purposes following deprovisioning.

Triggering & escalation mechanics:
- Customer initiation: Customer may initiate deprovisioning or sequester by sending a written notice to the Redwood security contact and account owner with the factual basis. The template notice must include: summary of grounds, affected project(s), and desired outcome (restore, permanent deletion, escrow transfer).
- Redwood initiation: Redwood may initiate pre-emptive sequester where there is reasonable belief of exfiltration, unlawful processing, or critical operational risk. Redwood will notify Customer within 4 business hours of initiation (unless notification would materially impede security response).
- Immediate actions upon trigger (first 0-4 hours): suspend API tokens and non-critical consoles; enforce read-only mode for suspected buckets/volumes; snapshot relevant storage volumes; start audit log preservation process.

Access removal and attestations:
- Account & credential revocation: Redwood will revoke or rotate all identified service credentials and user accounts with access to affected resources within the first 8 hours unless otherwise agreed.
- Least-privilege verification: Redwood will generate and share an access ledger (list of accounts/roles that had access) within 24 hours for Customer review.
- Attestation of actions: Redwood will provide a signed written attestation within 72 hours confirming steps taken, affected artifact IDs, and cryptographic hashes for preserved snapshots.

Data snapshots, custody window, and transfer options:
- Snapshots: Redwood will take encrypted snapshots of data and model artifacts required to reconstruct the environment for forensic or reinstatement purposes. Each snapshot will be labeled with timestamp, canonical identifier, and SHA-256 hash.
- Custody window default: 90 days post-deprovisioning (negotiable). During the custody window Redwood will store snapshots in encrypted cold storage under the Customer key when technically feasible.
- Transfer/escrow options: At Customer request (and subject to export controls and legal holds), Redwood will: (a) transfer encrypted snapshots to a Customer-specified S3 bucket or transfer agent; or (b) deposit encrypted snapshots with an independent escrow provider. Transfer deadlines and egress fees should be negotiated (see Fees & costs).

Sequester vs. service continuity decisions:
- Read-only vs full suspension: For less severe events, the parties will prefer read-only sequester. For high-severity events (confirmed exfiltration, active compromise) the default is full suspension of serving for affected resources.
- Canary restore path: Redwood agrees to provide a test-only restoration environment (isolated VPC) for joint validation before full-service restore; timing for canary validation is target 5 business days after transfer if Customer elects.

Chain of custody & forensic preservation:
- Forensic handling: Snapshots and logs will be preserved with a documented chain-of-custody record, including personnel actions, hashes, access approvals, and time-synced audit trail.
- Independent review: Customer may engage an independent, mutually agreed third-party forensic firm at Customer cost to validate preservation and integrity.

Evidence and audit rights:
- Audit scope: Customer shall have the right to audit metadata and chain-of-custody records associated with preserved snapshots. Audits may be remote or on-site with prior notice, limited to non-disruptive review during the custody window.
- Privileged material: Redwood retains the right to redact internal privileged materials from any shared forensic artifacts, subject to good-faith negotiation and a dispute escalation path.

Restoration, deletion, and proof of destruction:
- Restoration request: Customer may request restore of preserved snapshots within the custody window. Requests must specify datasets/artifacts and desired target environment. Redwood will provide timeline estimates within 48 hours of a restoration request.
- Deletion request: Customer may request permanent deletion at any time; Redwood will securely delete all backups and confirm deletion with signed certificate within 30 days, subject to any legal hold.
- Proof of destruction: Redwood will provide cryptographic proof-of-destruction (e.g., certificate plus destruction hash log) where technical controls permit.

Cost allocation & fees:
- Incident deprovisioning work: The first incident per 12-month period will be absorbed by Redwood for incidents caused by Redwood; otherwise, time-and-materials fees apply per agreed schedule.
- Egress & escrow: Standard egress fees and third-party escrow fees apply for snapshot transfer; exceptions may be negotiated for enterprise customers.

Dispute resolution & emergency override:
- Emergency override: If Customer reasonably believes Redwood is withholding critical data preservation evidence, Customer may seek emergency injunctive relief; parties agree to engage in expedited good-faith mediation before civil action where possible.
- Governing law & venue: [Placeholder — typically State/Country].

Operational playbook (practical checklist for engineering & security):
This section is intentionally operational and may be annexed to runbooks.
- T+0: Trigger notice received or internal detection
  * Lockdown: revoke console access for non-essential roles
  * Begin immutable snapshot job (list target identifiers)
  * Notify legal and account teams
- T+1 (within 4 hours):
  * Snapshot complete — compute hashes, write chain-of-custody entry
  * Begin transfer to cold storage/customer escrow on request
  * Begin internal root-cause forensic captures (memory, network flows)
- T+24:
  * Provide access ledger and signed attestation to Customer
  * Legal and security sync call with Customer scheduled
- T+72:
  * Final attestation delivered; retention schedule and fees confirmed

Negotiation notes / open items (for redlines):
- Custody window length (default 90d) — Customer may request longer retention for regulated workloads.
- Proof-of-destruction format — cryptographic standard and certificate template to be agreed.
- Egress fee waiver for enterprise pilots or if Redwood is at-fault.
- Escrow provider list and transfer SLA targets.

Notes to internal reviewers:
- This draft blends legal protections with a pragmatic runbook to reduce finger-pointing in high-pressure incidents. Keep options for automated snapshotting in product docs.
- Coordinate with Product (Private Deployments) on technical feasibility of Customer-keyed snapshot storage for on-prem and VPC deployments.
- Validate export-control checks for cross-border snapshot transfers.
